strengths: Targets an important problem and offers an intuitive macro-level planning and micro-level self-reflection framework on a unified text-image backbone.
The architecture, attention masks, and multimodal trajectories are illustrated clearly, and the approximate scale and construction of the synthetic training data are partially documented.

Evaluation covers five established generation and editing benchmarks. Uni-CoT is competitive among open-source systems, including 0.83 on GenEval and 68.00 on KRIS, while qualitative examples demonstrate useful iterative corrections.
The limitations section candidly acknowledges the current focus on sequential decomposition and image-generation tasks.
weaknesses: The central causal claims lack adequate ablations. The paper does not separately evaluate macro planning, micro-level objectives, attention masks, or DPO; “Uni-CoT Init” is insufficiently defined; and there is no same-backbone, inference-compute-matched iterative-refinement baseline. Extra generation and editing passes could explain much of the improvement.

The claimed computational savings are not demonstrated through FLOPs, latency, memory, throughput, GPU-hours, or direct comparison with BAGEL. Attention masking alone does not necessarily reduce computation without an appropriate sparse implementation.

The method is incomplete and insufficiently reproducible. Two of the three proposed macro strategies remain future work, the supplement explicitly defers reinforcement-learning details, and preference construction, the visual DPO objective, several hyperparameters, training duration, inference settings, stopping rules, model scale, and checkpoints are missing.

The experiments assess final-image quality rather than reasoning coherence, grounding, or trajectory faithfulness. No text-and-vision understanding task is evaluated despite the broad title, and the Nano-Banana section is an uncontrolled qualitative comparison without matched inputs or quantitative results.

The baseline study omits several closely related reasoning-based generation methods cited by the paper, does not match test-time computation, and emphasizes open-source comparisons even though GPT-4o remains substantially stronger on WISE and RISE. Error bars and significance tests are absent, and several improvements over the initialization or base model are small.

Training-data provenance is vague: prompts come from incompletely specified sources, while GPT-4o, Qwen, and BAGEL are used to generate or evaluate trajectories. There is no benchmark-overlap audit, licensing discussion, evaluator protocol, or analysis of teacher/evaluator bias.

Novelty is limited because hierarchical task decomposition, self-reflection, and localized context are established techniques. The MDP framing adds little formal substance: there is no transition, policy, or value analysis, and the proposed objectives largely reduce to supervised next-step prediction.

Technical and presentation inconsistencies reduce confidence: the main and supplementary cross-entropy equations disagree on the sign, reward prediction is described inconsistently as textual judgment versus scalar regression, and the manuscript contains duplicate labels, numerous typographical errors, and future-version placeholders.

weaknesses: The proposed method is incomplete relative to its framing. Only sequential decomposition and self-reflection are implemented; parallel decomposition and progressive refinement are described as contributions but explicitly deferred to future work.

The MDP formulation is largely terminological. There is no rigorous transition model, policy, Bellman-style objective, or analysis of the Markov assumption. The reward is inconsistently described as a scalar and a textual judgment, and the stopping rule and maximum number of reflection steps are unspecified.

Critical reinforcement-learning and DPO details are explicitly withheld for a future version. Preference construction, objectives, coefficients, training schedule, and the respective effects of SFT and DPO are absent, preventing technical verification and reproduction.

The central efficiency claim is unsupported. The paper reports neither complexity analysis nor FLOPs, memory, latency, throughput, GPU-hours, or matched training comparisons. Attention masking alone does not necessarily reduce computation under dense attention, and stating that training uses eight A100 GPUs is insufficient evidence.

Ablations are inadequate. The initial-versus-final comparison cannot isolate the effects of hierarchical decomposition, macro and micro masks, auxiliary MDP objectives, self-reflection, DPO, additional training data, or the number of refinement rounds.

Comparisons are not test-time-compute matched: Uni-CoT can generate and evaluate multiple intermediate images, while baselines appear to be evaluated one-shot. Iterative or best-of-N controls and comparisons with the closest reasoning-driven generation methods are missing.

Final-image benchmark scores do not establish that the exposed trajectories are faithful, grounded, or causally useful reasoning. There is no evaluation of plan correctness, trajectory consistency, interpretability, or multimodal understanding tasks.
